foundational_validity_assessment: Foundationally valid (PCAST 2016); also simple two-person mixtures
error_rate_evidence: PCAST: chance-match probabilities estimable from population databases and extremely low; no single lab error rate given; contamination/handling errors are the practical risk
key_concerns: Source-level only: does not show how/when DNA was deposited; contamination; transfer
relevant_standards: ANSI/ASB Standard 040 (2019, 1st ed.); ISO/IEC 17025:2017
teen_education_suitability: High (13+ for exclusion logic; 16+ for transfer)

foundational_validity_assessment: PCAST 2016: subjective interpretation not valid; PG software valid only within limited range (3 contributors, minor >=20%). NIST IR 8351 (2024): reliability is a matter of degree; insufficient public data
error_rate_evidence: Interlaboratory studies show wide variation; LRs differ by software/analyst; proficiency tests mostly simple samples
key_concerns: Subjectivity and context (Dror & Hampikian 2011); LR assigned not measured; activity-level questions unaddressed
relevant_standards: ANSI/ASB Standard 040; ISFG 2018 propositions guidance; ISO 21043-4:2025
teen_education_suitability: Medium (18+ as concept: 'more contributors = more uncertainty')

foundational_validity_assessment: No single validity verdict; NIST IR 8351 (2024) and ISFG (2018) stress significant knowledge gaps on transfer/persistence
error_rate_evidence: Transfer rates vary widely by conditions (van Oorschot et al. 2019 review); no general error rate
key_concerns: Secondary transfer; background DNA; over-reading of a source match as activity
relevant_standards: ISO 21043-4:2025; ENFSI 2015 guideline (activity-level propositions)

foundational_validity_assessment: Foundationally valid subjective method with substantial false-positive rate (PCAST 2016); NRC 2009 said ACE-V not specific enough to be validated
error_rate_evidence: Ulery et al. 2011: FP 0.1%, FN 7.5% (169 examiners); PCAST upper bounds up to 1 in 306 (FBI study) and 1 in 18 (other lab study)
key_concerns: Contextual bias (Dror 2006); examiner disagreement on suitability; testimony overstatement
relevant_standards: OSAC Friction Ridge standards on Registry (not individually verified); ISO/IEC 17025

foundational_validity_assessment: Not assessed by PCAST; NIST human-factors report (2020/2021) recommends systemic safeguards; black-box study 2022
error_rate_evidence: Hicklin et al. 2022: 3.1% erroneous 'written by' on non-mated, 1.1% erroneous 'not written by' on mated; twins 8.7%
key_concerns: Twins/similar writers; training level; no consensus on probability expression; Latin-script data only
relevant_standards: ANSI/ASB Standard 011 (scope of expertise; edition not verified); NISTIR 8282r1

foundational_validity_assessment: Fell short of foundational validity in 2016 (PCAST: one appropriate black-box study); contested by DOJ 2021
error_rate_evidence: PCAST: FP ~1 in 66 (upper bound 1 in 46) in Ames study; Monson et al. 2023: FP ~0.66% bullets, ~0.93% cartridge cases; strongly dependent on handling of inconclusives (Dorfman & Valliant 2022)
key_concerns: Inconclusive-rate debate; closed-set designs underestimate error; error concentrated in few examiners
relevant_standards: ASB Standard 096 (ammunition documentation; edition not verified); OSAC Firearms & Toolmarks subcommittee (14 Registry items)
teen_education_suitability: Low for teens (weapon topic); toolmark-on-lock analogue acceptable 16+

method: Toolmark analogue (fictional tool on fictional lock/wood)
foundational_validity_assessment: Educational analogue only; inherits firearms/toolmark uncertainty
error_rate_evidence: Use fictional examiner-error data in game; do not cite real rates as if for this analogue
key_concerns: Must not drift into weapon content; class vs individual characteristics
relevant_standards: None specific

foundational_validity_assessment: Not supported: PCAST 2016 far from foundational validity; NIST IR 8352 (2023): none of three premises supported
error_rate_evidence: PCAST: observed FP rates typically above 10%; NIST: in one study only 8% of cases reached 90% analyst agreement on key questions
key_concerns: Skin distortion; uniqueness unproven; examiner disagreement on whether injury is a bite
relevant_standards: No OSAC-endorsed method for bitemark identification (status to confirm)
teen_education_suitability: High as a 'discredited method' case study using clay/fruit analogue (13+); never as valid evidence

foundational_validity_assessment: Foundational validity not established (PCAST 2016 review of DOJ document)
error_rate_evidence: FBI 2002 mtDNA re-examination: 9 of 80 (11%) microscopically indistinguishable hairs came from different people
key_concerns: Overstated testimony historically; listed by Innocence Project among problem disciplines
relevant_standards: OSAC Trace Materials standards exist for hair/fibre examination (not individually verified)

foundational_validity_assessment: Not scientifically valid for associating a print with a specific shoe via identifying marks (PCAST 2016); class characteristics not assessed
error_rate_evidence: No appropriate black-box studies as of 2016-2017; later studies not verified in-session
key_concerns: Class vs individual characteristics confusion; manufacturing volume unknown
relevant_standards: OSAC Footwear & Tire subcommittee standards (not individually verified)
teen_education_suitability: High at class level (13+: 'how many shoes share this tread?')

foundational_validity_assessment: No PCAST verdict; class-level associations; value depends on population/background data (Roux et al. 2015)
error_rate_evidence: No general error rate; frequency data case- and region-specific
key_concerns: Over-interpretation of class similarity; persistence/loss; background levels
relevant_standards: OSAC Trace Materials (34 Registry items at fetch; specific titles not verified); ENFSI evaluative guideline

foundational_validity_assessment: Generally accepted analytical identification when SWGDRUG minimum standards met (v8.2, 2024)
error_rate_evidence: Presumptive (colour) tests have false positives; Morgan 2023 found reliance on unconfirmed presumptive tests among wrongful-conviction factors
key_concerns: Presumptive vs confirmatory confusion; safety: no drug-specific content for teens
relevant_standards: SWGDRUG Recommendations v8.2 (2024); ISO/IEC 17025
teen_education_suitability: Medium (13+ only as abstract 'Substance X' logic)

foundational_validity_assessment: NRC 2004 (Forensic Analysis: Weighing Bullet Lead Evidence): measurement technique sound but inferences overstated; not unique; cannot link to a box or give source probability; Innocence Project lists CBLA among flawed disciplines
error_rate_evidence: FBI claimed 1 in 2,500 false-match probability via undocumented 2-SD overlap; NRC criticised the statistical grouping (chaining) and noted a box may contain up to 14 compositional groups
key_concerns: Accurate measurement mistaken for valid source inference; missing distribution data; weapon-adjacent
relevant_standards: None (discontinued practice per secondary sources; not verified)

foundational_validity_assessment: Validated methods required before casework (SWGTOX 2013; ASB toxicology standards 098/113)
error_rate_evidence: No general error rate in verified sources; method-specific validation parameters
key_concerns: Detection is not causation; 'not detected' is not 'not present'; safety-critical topic
relevant_standards: SWGTOX 2013 (possibly superseded by ANSI/ASB 036 - unverified); ANSI/ASB 098, 113
teen_education_suitability: Low-medium (16+, interpretation principle only; no substances/doses)

foundational_validity_assessment: Accepted as interval estimation with stated uncertainty (Henssge & Madea 2004 review)
error_rate_evidence: Error expressed as confidence intervals that widen with time and unknown conditions
key_concerns: Environmental variables; single-method over-precision
relevant_standards: None verified in-session
teen_education_suitability: Medium (13+ via non-human cooling analogue; no body content)

foundational_validity_assessment: Expert judgement integrating medical and investigative information; bias concern raised by Dror et al. 2021 (contested)
error_rate_evidence: No general error rate; inter-pathologist variability documented in contested study
key_concerns: Context needed but can bias; sensitive topics (child deaths, suicide)
relevant_standards: None verified in-session

foundational_validity_assessment: Accepted with population-appropriate, validated methods (Christensen & Crowder 2009)
error_rate_evidence: Method-specific; dental imaging age estimation reviewed systematically (Marroquin et al. 2017)
key_concerns: Reference-population mismatch; contextual bias (Nakhaeizadeh et al. 2014); cultural sensitivity
relevant_standards: OSAC Anthropology subcommittee (11 Registry items at fetch; titles not verified)

method: Digital forensic acquisition and artefact analysis
foundational_validity_assessment: Reliable when appropriately applied (NIST IR 8354, 2022)
error_rate_evidence: Tool-specific; NIST CFTT/CFReDS used to test tools; no single error rate
key_concerns: Not all evidence found; deleted-file recovery noise; artefact meaning changes with software versions; user attribution
relevant_standards: SWGDE documents (12 on OSAC Registry); ISO/IEC 27037 (referenced by ISO 21043-2; not verified)

foundational_validity_assessment: Principles set in SWGDE consensus documents; no NIST foundation review verified
error_rate_evidence: No general error rate verified
key_concerns: Enhancement cannot create absent detail; low-resolution identification limits; generative-AI images
relevant_standards: SWGDE imaging/photography/video documents (titles not verified)

foundational_validity_assessment: Royal Society/RSE primer (2017) explains use and limitations for courts
error_rate_evidence: Not quantified in verified sources
key_concerns: Low image quality; within-person variability; limited population data
relevant_standards: None verified

method: Crime scene documentation and chain of custody
foundational_validity_assessment: Process standard rather than validity question (ISO 21043-2:2018, under revision; NIJ 2013 guide)
error_rate_evidence: Errors are procedural (loss, contamination, incomplete records)
key_concerns: Selective documentation; tunnel vision; contamination
relevant_standards: ISO 21043-2:2018 (stage 90.92 to be revised); NIJ guide NCJ 243598

foundational_validity_assessment: Recommended framework in Europe (ENFSI 2015) and in ISO 21043-4:2025; not universally adopted (US practice)
error_rate_evidence: LRs are assigned and can vary between analysts/software (NIST IR 8351)
key_concerns: Verbal scales misunderstood; transposed conditional; proposition level choice
relevant_standards: ENFSI Guideline v3.0 (2015); ISO 21043-4:2025; ISO 21043-5 (not verified)

method: Context management / Linear Sequential Unmasking (LSU, LSU-E)
foundational_validity_assessment: Procedural safeguard recommended by NIST human-factors reports; limited empirical outcome data
error_rate_evidence: Effectiveness in casework not quantified in verified sources
key_concerns: Practicality (handwriting features not predefinable); adoption varies
relevant_standards: NISTIR 7842; NISTIR 8282r1; FSR Code of Practice v2 (contents not read)

foundational_validity_assessment: ISO/IEC 17025:2017 (confirmed 2023) is the accreditation basis; does not by itself validate methods
error_rate_evidence: Proficiency tests often easier than casework (NIST IR 8351)
key_concerns: Accreditation mistaken for proof of correctness
relevant_standards: ISO/IEC 17025:2017; FSR Code of Practice v2 (2025, England & Wales); OSAC Registry
